title: Sharp and flat drums
summary: He explains that sharp drums are tuned tight while flat drums will not hold the tuning, and shows his own drums.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well, no, they got drums sharp and they got drums flat.
Yeah, I've got a flat drum right there now. And I have a sharp one. I've got two sharp ones.
That's what I don't know what you mean for sure about sharp. You mean it's a deeper drum? Or do you tune it up, stretch the head up tighter? No, you can tune it up.
Tune it up, that's what I thought. Tune it up good and tight.
Tune it up dear. Now, you said that one right behind the lamp there is a flat drum.
Yeah, it ain't no sharp drums.
It won't tune up to sharp one?
No, it ain't going to hold it. Mm-hm. That's right. Tune it up, but it ain't going to hold it.
Would it have the same depth of the shell?
Yeah, I've got my black drum what I use in the fuse. Mm-hm. It's sharp as a race.
